 "explanation": "The unit responds mainly to quadruped mammals, especially dogs and wolves, seen standing in full-body side or three-quarter view. It responds more weakly to other animals with a similar body layout, such as a weasel, a zebra, and gazelles, and to a lesser extent a bird in side profile.",
 "evidence": "Most of the top 20 images are dogs or wolves (#1-5, #7-8, #10, #12-18), and nearly all show the whole body from the side. The non-dog images (sandpiper #6, zebra #9, weasel #11, gazelles #20) score lower, at activations 7-8, and share the side-profile animal shape.",
 "missing_data": "Activations on non-canid quadrupeds such as cats, horses, and cattle, and on close-up dog faces versus full bodies, would show whether the unit is selective for dogs or for the general quadruped body shape.",
 "confidence": 0.7}
